title: function-calling-parse-debug-scratchpad-jordan
content:
Goal: track investigation into repeated parse failures when using function/tool-calling mode with the hosted API. Personal scratchpad - rough, partial notes, commands tried, errors, hypotheses, and next steps.

Summary of symptom:
- Intermittent JSON parsing failures on responses that are supposed to be strict JSON for downstream tooling. Failures observed in both SDK (python) and curl-based calls. Mostly manifests as `JSONDecodeError: Expecting value` or `Unexpected token` when parsing response body.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions with function_call schema enforced (we call tools via the model’s function_call output).
- Frequency: ~3-7% of calls in canary traffic; seems correlated with higher temperature and longer max_tokens.

Repro steps (local):
1) Minimal curl that recreated parse error about 2024-11-02 16:20 UTC:
   curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"model":"open-like-2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Generate JSON for customer contact: name, email"}],"function_call":{"name":"upsert_contact","arguments_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"email":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name","email"]}},"temperature":0.9,"max_tokens":500}' \n   > out.txt; echo "---RESPONSE---"; cat out.txt
   Observed: sometimes response begins with a stray newline and then a JSON object; sometimes the model returns leading commentary ("Sure — here's the object") before the JSON.

2) SDK (python) snippet that raised JSONDecodeError:
   from redwood import RedwoodClient
   client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
   res = client.chat.create(model='open-like-2', messages=[{"role":"user","content":"..."}], function_call={"name":"upsert_contact","arguments_schema":...}, temperature=0.8)
   body = res.text
   obj = json.loads(body)  # -> JSONDecodeError on some runs

Observed response samples (raw):
- Good (expected):
  {"name":"Alex Morgan","email":"alex.morgan@example.com"}

- Bad (leading text):
  "Sure, here's the object you can use:\n  {\"name\": \"Alex Morgan\", \"email\": \"alex.morgan@example.com\"}\n  "

- Bad (malformed JSON due to trailing comma):
  {"name":"Alex Morgan", "email":"alex.morgan@example.com",}

- Bad (split streaming chunk boundary):
  chunk1: "{\"name\": \"Alex Mo"\n  chunk2: "rgan\", \"email\": \"alex@example.com\"}"
  If the client concatenates incorrectly or a chunk boundary is lost we sometimes see an embedded escape sequence.

Commands/flags tried during testing:
- Set temperature=0.0 -> reduced but did not eliminate errors (approx 1% remaining).
- Forced `function_call":{"name":"upsert_contact","arguments":"{}"}` vs letting model decide. No change.
- Added "system" prompt with explicit instruction: "ONLY RETURN A JSON OBJECT, NO EXPLANATION, NO LEADING TEXT." Reduced leading commentary but not 100%.
- Switched to single-turn vs multi-turn contexts to minimize stray tokens. Small improvement.
- Increased `max_new_tokens`/`max_tokens` to ensure model doesn't cut off; helps with truncation-related parse issues but not commentary.
- Try parse-resilient code: locate first `{` in body and attempt to json.loads from that index - workaround but brittle.

Hypotheses:
1) Model sometimes emits assistant-level commentary before JSON (verbal confirmation) despite instructions - classic LM behavior. Higher temperature increases it.
2) Streaming/chunking reassembly bug in client or proxy that mangles quotes/escapes across chunk boundaries. Evidence: malformed JSON appears aligned with stream edges in logs.
3) Function_call schema/interpretation mismatch: the model thinks it's allowed to "explain" its output. If our function_call enforcement layer is not configured to strip assistant text, model can include both text and arguments.
4) Occasional server-side trimming or insertion (e.g., rate limiting banners or internal debug messages) - low probability but need to rule out.

Trace data & breadcrumbs (partial):
- Canary run ids (redacted): run-20241102-16:18, run-20241103-09:22, run-20241104-14:05
- Request id examples: rwd-req-ef9a1c, rwd-req-f12b3a (see SRE logs).
- Logged response bodies saved to s3: s3://redwood-debug/function-call/2024-11-02/run-ef9a1c/response-1.txt
- Observed stacktrace (python client): JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) -> indicates body starts with non-JSON or empty.

Investigation steps done so far (internal):
- Validated client-side concat and decoding logic on SDK: added logging to dump raw bytes and verify character encoding (utf-8). No encoding anomalies found.
- Instrumented streaming reassembly path: added checksums per-chunk to confirm order/consistency. No checksum mismatches in the canary sample we examined, but one case showed a chunk arriving with leading "\\n".

- Reproduced locally by running large batch with temperature sweep; saw higher failure rate at temp >= 0.7.
- Replayed problematic request through staging with full request/response capture; staging showed same leading commentary occasionally.
- Asked model-onboarding team: checked the model's function_call behavior in evaluation harness - model sometimes returns text + arguments when not forced.

Immediate mitigations (practical):
- Add a robust post-parse cleanup in the SDK: try to locate the JSON substring (first '{' to last '}') and attempt to parse. Keep as fallback only.
- Enforce temperature=0.0 for production tools that need strict JSON (conservative).
- Add a server-side filter that strips leading non-JSON tokens when function_call is expected. Needs product sign-off.

Longer-term fixes to validate (owners):
- Product/ML: ensure function_call enforcement (model behavior) is updated/finetuned to never emit free text when function_call is used. (Owner: model-onboarding).
- Runtime: add strict framing for function_call outputs in streaming mode (e.g., explicit token that starts the JSON payload or using framing messages). (Owner: serving-runtime).
- SDK: expose a safe_parse option that implements resilient parsing with clear telemetry when falling back. (Owner: developer-experience).

Notes for next debugging pass:
- Capture full raw byte stream for two failing requests and compare chunk boundaries and timestamps; include client sdk version, OS, and any proxies.
- Run AB test on server-side stripping rule for canary and measure false positives (cases where leading text was intentionally part of response).
- Reproduce the trailing-comma case separately; might be model output formatting, or occasionally a post-processing function inserting a trailing comma when serializing.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Add SDK fallback parser + telemetry (Jordan) - due 2024-11-12
- [ ] Open internal PR for server-side leading-text strip policy (eng-runtime) - assign to Ashwin
- [ ] Coordinate with model-onboarding to run a focused eval that measures "clean JSON" rate across temperatures and prompt templates (Maya)
- [ ] Collect 10 failing raw responses and upload to s3 debug bucket (done: see linked s3 path above)

Random notes / stray ideas:
- Could consider a tiny framing token like "<JSON>... </JSON>" emitted by system prompt and stripped by client; needs escape analysis in downstream tooling.
- For streaming, include chunk-level metadata (seq numbers, checksum) so client can validate reassembly.
- Consider an API-level header (X-Strict-Output: json) that enforces no extra commentary at the gateway; gateway can apply soft filters.

Scratchpad end. More formal incident writeup (if needed) will be assembled once we have the 10 raw failing examples consolidated and SDK telemetry in place.

Contact: Jordan Lee (jordan.lee@redwoodelc.com) - ping in #runtime-debug for fast sync.
